The appendix deliberately covers “alte Etyma aus allen Dialekten” of European Romani rather than only the southeastern varieties of the dictionary proper, and cites every word in the shape it carries as a main entry there\. rows.etymology: 49. Kho. ċrˈex ‘spark’, Kal. ċrek ‘sparks’ — Wkh. ċrax, ċerax ‘spark’, Yid. ċərox ‘spark’ and “similar forms are found also in other Ir. languages” (Morgenstierne [1936]) — perhaps Sant. cerceʈeʔc ‘sparks to fly, as when thorns are burning, or when iron at white heat is hammered’ and ceʈe ‘sparks, as from thorns when burning’ which has perhaps a cognate in Khmer crɨc ‘cracking, crackling sound’. There are no really unambiguous parallels between the Indo-Iranian and the Austro-Asiatic forms.
